rules.heading: Build the simplest thing that answers the question
rules.nativeFeature: OpenTelemetry metrics export (claude_code.cost.usage, .token.usage, .code_edit_tool.decision, .commit.count, .pull_request.count) and the statusline JSON fields (cost.total_cost_usd, context_window.*)
rules.evidence: The rule's tactic "check whether the platform already measures the thing before modelling it" has a concrete harness instance in the new areas: once CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 is set, the harness already exports session, cost, token, code-edit-decision, commit, and pull-request metrics, and a statusline script already receives cost.total_cost_usd, cost.total_duration_ms, and context_window fields on stdin while "the status line runs locally and does not consume API tokens". Nothing in plan mode, headless mode, or cost reporting expresses a simplicity posture, so there is no duplication and no conflict; the rule adds a design stance the harness has none of, and its existing generic wording already points at these primitives without naming them.

rules.heading: Search public prior art before building a tool, and record what you did not adopt
rules.nativeFeature: Plan mode ("analyze before you edit with plan mode"), plus the plan review and approval flow
rules.evidence: Plan mode is the native primitive for exactly this phase: "Claude reads files, runs shell commands to explore, and writes a plan, but does not edit your source. Except in sessions with bypass permissions available, edits stay blocked until you approve the plan." It supplies the enforcement the rule's evaluation step wants and the rule never cites. It duplicates nothing the rule asks for: plan mode has no notion of prior art, imposes no search before building, and persists nothing (approving a plan exits plan mode and at most auto-generates a session title), so the rule's durable not-adopted record under docs/decisions/ is additive scope. The floor is also conditional, since in a session with bypass permissions available "Claude is still instructed to plan without editing, but a file edit or shell command it attempts during planning runs without prompting" - a posture the rule should carry rather than assume.
rules.proposedWording:
## Search public prior art before building a tool, and record what you did not adopt

Look for an existing tool before writing one, and record what you evaluated and did not adopt with the case that decided it, because an unrecorded rejection gets re-litigated.
Run the search in the harness planning phase, where edits stay blocked until a plan is approved, and hold that posture yourself in a session where the block does not apply, because the plan is not the record.
Judge a system against its own rules first, then against current external guidance with the sources listed.
Anchor: a record under `docs/decisions/` naming the candidates, the deciding case, and the adopt or not-adopt call
Receipts: `docs/handbook/engineering.md#search-public-prior-art-before-building-a-tool-and-record-what-you-did-not-adopt`

rules.heading: Record a significant decision as a numbered, immutable record
rules.evidence: Nothing in plan mode, headless mode, or cost and telemetry reporting records a decision durably. The plan-mode approval flow is the closest thing and is explicitly a live user choice, not an artifact: "Approving a plan exits plan mode and switches the session to the permission mode each approve option describes", with the only persisted residue an auto-generated session title. Headless mode moves in the opposite direction, with --no-session-persistence disabling saving the session to disk at all. No native mechanism numbers, supersedes, or immutably retains a decision, so the rule stands alone and conflicts with nothing.

rules.heading: Make a measuring instrument reproducible
rules.nativeFeature: --bare non-interactive mode (headless) and the client-side cost figure reported by --output-format json, /usage, and the statusline (with the modelPricing managed setting and the data residency multiplier)
rules.evidence: Headless mode supplies the reproducibility floor the rule wants whenever the instrument itself drives an agent: without --bare, "a -p session runs the hooks in a project's .claude/settings.json and connects the servers in its .mcp.json, even in a folder you've never trusted", so an ambient local hook or server silently perturbs a run, while --bare "skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md" and "is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls". Cost reporting adds a second, unnamed reproducibility hazard for the rule's "modelled number" clause: the harness "computes every cost figure it shows developers at list price" locally, an admin-only modelPricing managed setting "changes what Claude Code reports, not what Anthropic charges", and a data residency response has its list price multiplied before it reaches the same figure the status line and --max-budget-usd read. Two machines can therefore print different costs for the same run. The rule duplicates none of this and contradicts none of it; it adds the requirement to pin the invocation and to record the basis.
rules.proposedWording:
## Make a measuring instrument reproducible

Seed the sampling so two initializing runs are byte-identical, because a baseline fingerprint nobody can reproduce means nothing.
Regenerate a fixture from its source under a seed instead of curating it, treat a holdout as spent once it has been validated against, require a byte-identical parity diff when a formula changes, log every assumption behind a modelled number with the command that re-pulls it, move the baseline in the change that moves the numbers with the why in the pull request, and read growth in reviewer-corrected labels as decay of the key rather than improvement.
When the instrument drives an agent, pin the bare non-interactive invocation that skips ambient discovery, so a stray local hook or server cannot move the numbers, and record the pricing basis beside any cost the harness reports, because that figure is computed locally and a configured rate or a residency multiplier moves it without moving the bill.
Anchor: seeded regeneration asserted byte-identical in `tests/`
Receipts: `docs/handbook/engineering.md#make-a-measuring-instrument-reproducible`

notes:
Scope call: four headings matched the filter (simplest, prior art, decision, measuring/reproducible). "Show the ratio and the sample" contains neither "measuring" nor "reproducible" in its heading, so I left it out even though the cost-estimate facts (list-price computation, modelPricing, residency multiplier, background token usage under a fixed per-session ceiling) bear on it directly; it is the strongest candidate in this file for a follow-up pass against the cost area.

Judgment calls I was unsure about:
- Rule 1 (simplest): I marked COMPLEMENT rather than UNIQUE because its own tactic line already tells the reader to check whether the platform measures a thing first, and the telemetry and statusline facts are a live instance of that. I still chose keep over a reword, because naming this harness's metric names inside a portable engineering rule narrows a deliberately general instruction. If the owner prefers concreteness over portability, the reword would add one clause pointing at the exporter and the statusline payload before writing a counter.
- Rule 3 (prior art): the reword is the one place I think a cite genuinely changes behavior, since it names where the search happens and warns that the edit block is absent in a bypass-permissions session. I deliberately did not name plan mode by its literal product name in the proposed prose, to keep the rule readable in a repo that vendors it outside this harness; if the house style prefers exact product names, "the harness planning phase" should become the literal mode name.
- Rule 4: one possible tension I did not rate a CONFLICT. The rule demands byte-identical runs under a seed. If someone reads "measuring instrument" to include the agent run itself, the harness offers no seed and byte-identical agent output is unattainable, and a json result carries a session id and a cost estimate that vary per run. I read the rule as governing fixture and sampling regeneration, not model output, so I treated it as a scope ambiguity rather than a contradiction of documented behavior. Worth a clarifying clause if the owner intends the broader reading.
- Rule 2: plan mode is adjacent (a decision point with no artifact) but not a counterpart, so I applied the instruction's default and marked it UNIQUE with nativeFeature "none in the new areas".

No rule in scope duplicated or fought a native mechanism, so there are no delete, declare-intentional-duplicate, or resolve-conflict actions here.
